vulnerabilities.description: Apache Tomcat authentication bypass where OCSP validation soft-fails even when soft-fail is explicitly disabled, allowing revoked client certificates to authenticate.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: Server-side TLS authentication vulnerability. Liquibase never starts a Tomcat server or binds an HTTPS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency present in the distribution JAR but never initialized.

analysis.detail: Authentication bypass due to CLIENT_CERT soft fail misconfiguration in Tomcat's OCSP validation. Requires an active HTTPS connector configured with CLIENT_CERT authentication and an OCSP responder. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No connector, no authenticator, no OCSP — the code is inert.

HTTP request/response smuggling via invalid chunk extension in Tomcat HTTP/1.1 parser. Requires an active HTTP listener processing inbound requests. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; the HTTP parser is never invoked.

Denial of service via integer overflow in Tomcat multipart upload file size limit validation. Requires sending a crafted multipart HTTP upload to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never processes inbound HTTP requests or multipart uploads.

Denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption in Tomcat HTTP/2 stream management. Requires an HTTP/2 client connecting to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and never binds a network port.

Path traversal and potential RCE via regression in Tomcat Rewrite Valve URL normalization. Requires an HTTP request to a running Tomcat server with the Rewrite Valve configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never configures the Rewrite Valve, and never accepts HTTP requests.

vulnerabilities.description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117. Older, unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version [FIXED_VERSION], which fixes the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to enable Tomcat WebDAV handling. Upgrade tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 or later if WebDAV support is added.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable Tomcat WebDAV LOCK and PROPFIND handlers require WebDAV servlet/configuration that is not present in the license utility.

analysis.detail: Unbounded request body reads in Tomcat WebDAV LOCK and PROPFIND handling affect Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. The license utility pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.21 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26, tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:52) through spring-boot-starter-web (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:60) and starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20), but no WebDAV servlet, WebDAV mapping, or PROPFIND/LOCK handler is configured in tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main or its application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1).

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat: HTTP/2 request headers were not validated, which may have triggered unexpected application behavior. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 10.0.0-M1 through 10.0.27. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to enable Tomcat HTTP/2 support.

ratings.justification: HTTP/2 is not enabled in the license utility, and tomcat-embed-core is pinned at the fixed version 11.0.22. Apache rates this CVE as Low severity in the Tomcat 11 security advisory.

analysis.detail: HTTP/2 request header validation gap in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires HTTP/2 connections to a running Tomcat server. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not enable HTTP/2 — application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) sets no server.http2.enabled property and declares no HTTP/2 connector, and the codebase contains no HTTP/2-specific Tomcat configuration. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26), so the fixed version is installed regardless.

vulnerabilities.description: Exposure of HTTP Authentication Header to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.2 through 9.0.117, 8.5.24 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.83 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to act as a Tomcat WebSocket client or server.

ratings.justification: Tomcat WebSocket APIs are not used by the license utility, and tomcat-embed-core is pinned at the fixed version 11.0.22. Apache rates this CVE as Low severity in the Tomcat 11 security advisory.

analysis.detail: Exposure of HTTP authentication headers to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires a WebSocket client following an HTTP redirect during authentication. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not use the Tomcat WebSocket client or server APIs. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no WebSocket endpoint definitions, and the codebase contains no ClientEndpoint/ServerEndpoint annotations or other WebSocket-related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

vulnerabilities.description: Authentication Bypass Issues vulnerability in digest authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to enable Tomcat digest authentication.

ratings.justification: Tomcat digest authentication is not configured in the license utility, and tomcat-embed-core is pinned at the fixed version 11.0.22. Apache rates this CVE as Moderate severity in the Tomcat 11 security advisory.

analysis.detail: Authentication bypass in Tomcat digest authentication, where any unknown user presenting the password "null" was authenticated. Affects Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires Tomcat to be configured to use DigestAuthenticator. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not configure any Tomcat realm or authenticator. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no realm/authenticator definitions, and the codebase contains no DigestAuthenticator or related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity in LockOutRealm in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for Liquibase Secure unless the license utility is customized to enable LockOutRealm or any other Tomcat realm.

ratings.justification: Tomcat realms (including LockOutRealm) are not configured in the license utility, and tomcat-embed-core is pinned at the fixed version 11.0.22. Apache rates this CVE as Low severity in the Tomcat 11 security advisory.

analysis.detail: LockOutRealm treats user names as case-sensitive, reducing its effectiveness against brute-force attacks. Affects Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires Tomcat to be configured to use LockOutRealm. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not configure any Tomcat realm. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no realm definitions, and the codebase contains no LockOutRealm or related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

Repo-wide searches found no source declaration for org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core; the only Tomcat references in the current tree are prior VEX notes. The active build declares unrelated dependencies such as httpcore5 5.4.3 in pom.xml:121-122 and jackson-core 2.22.1 in pom.xml:57,150-151 and community-extensions/liquibase-mongodb/pom.xml:48,90-92.

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Access Control, Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat leads to security constraint bypass if a constraint for a longer path is specified before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58, 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: Security-constraint evaluation only happens inside a running Tomcat servlet container processing deployed web.xml descriptors. Liquibase never starts a Tomcat server or deploys a web.xml, so the vulnerable code path is never exercised.

analysis.detail: Security constraint bypass when a `<security-constraint>` for a longer path is declared before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path in web.xml. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container evaluating security constraints against deployed web.xml descriptors. Liquibase is a CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No servlet container is started, so no security-constraint evaluation ever occurs.

TLS 1.3 cipher suite preference order not preserved in Tomcat's SSL connector configuration. Requires an active TLS connector performing cipher negotiation. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or binds a TLS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no TLS handshakes occur.

vulnerabilities.description: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator. If, before windowSize requests have been made, a client makes a DIGEST authenticated request with a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window then that request is replayable once only while the associated nonceCount remains within the replay window. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fix the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: DIGEST authentication replay only applies to a running Tomcat servlet container configured with a DIGEST authenticator. Liquibase never starts a Tomcat server and never configures DIGEST authentication, so the vulnerable code path is never exercised.

analysis.detail: Authentication bypass by capture-replay in Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator: a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window can be replayed once before it ages out. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with DIGEST authentication configured and processing inbound authenticated requests. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No DIGEST authenticator is ever configured or invoked.

vulnerabilities.description: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows the bypassing of a security constraint that limits user access to a resource via POST but not GET. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: FORM-authentication constraint bypass only applies to a running Tomcat servlet container with FORM authentication and a method-scoped security constraint configured. Liquibase never starts a Tomcat server and never configures FORM authentication, so the vulnerable code path is never exercised.

analysis.detail: Incorrect Authorization in Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows bypassing a security constraint that limits a user to POST access on a resource (not GET). Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with FORM authentication and a POST-only security constraint configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No FORM authenticator or security constraint is ever configured.

vulnerabilities.description: Occasional URL redirection to untrusted Site ('Open Redirect') vulnerability in Apache Tomcat via the LoadBalancerDrainingValve. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.18, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.52, from 9.0.0.M23 through 9.0.115, from 8.5.30 through 8.5.100. Other, unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.20, 10.1.53 or 9.0.116, which fix the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component configures Tomcat's LoadBalancerDrainingValve.

ratings.justification: The open redirect occurs only in LoadBalancerDrainingValve, which must be explicitly configured; no shipped component adds it, and the Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server.

analysis.detail: Occasional open redirect in Tomcat's LoadBalancerDrainingValve, fixed in Tomcat 11.0.20, 10.1.53 and 9.0.116. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 10.1.48 in 5.0.3, 11.0.15 in 5.1.0 and 11.0.18 in 5.1.1, all in range; 5.2.0 and later carry 11.0.22 or newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs LoadBalancerDrainingValve to be explicitly added to the server's pipeline, on a cluster node that a load balancer has put in the draining state. Tomcat never installs the valve by default and Spring Boot never configures it. The application sets no server properties, and none of its classes references a Tomcat valve, the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer.

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat due to an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66614. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.15 through 11.0.19, from 10.1.50 through 10.1.52, from 9.0.113 through 9.0.115. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.20, 10.1.53 or 9.0.116, which fix the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not run a Tomcat TLS connector with multiple virtual hosts or connector-level client certificate authentication.

ratings.justification: The SNI/Host check only matters for a TLS connector serving several virtual hosts with differing client certificate requirements. No Liquibase Secure component configures TLS, virtual hosts or connector-level client certificate authentication on Tomcat.

analysis.detail: Incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66614, fixed in Tomcat 11.0.20, 10.1.53 and 9.0.116: the strict check that the TLS SNI host name matches the HTTP Host header ignored differences in case, so it could be bypassed. It matters only when Tomcat terminates TLS itself with more than one SSLHostConfig, one of which requires client certificate authentication at the Connector while another does not. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. Only 5.1.0 (11.0.15) and 5.1.1 (11.0.18) carry an in-range version. 5.0.0 to 5.0.2 (10.1.34) and 5.0.3 (10.1.48) predate the strict SNI check, which the CVE-2025-66614 fix added in 10.1.50, and 5.2.0 and later carry 11.0.22 or newer, which include the fix. The application listens on a single plain HTTP connector with the Spring Boot defaults: it sets no server properties, ships no keystore, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API, an SSL bundle or a web server factory customizer.

vulnerabilities.description: Observable Timing Discrepancy vulnerability when comparing AJP secret in Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Older unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.22, 10.1.55 or 9.0.118 which fix the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component configures a Tomcat AJP connector.

ratings.justification: The timing discrepancy exists only in AJP secret comparison; no shipped component configures an AJP connector, and the Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server.

analysis.detail: Non-constant-time comparison of the AJP connector secret, a timing side channel that lets an attacker on the local network recover the secret; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.22, 10.1.55 and 9.0.118. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 10.1.48 in 5.0.3, 11.0.15 in 5.1.0 and 11.0.18 in 5.1.1, all in range; 5.2.0 and later carry 11.0.22 or newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs an AJP connector configured with a secret. Spring Boot exposes no property that enables AJP and starts only an HTTP connector; an AJP connector must be added in code through a web server factory customizer. The application sets no server properties, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API, a connector or a web server factory customizer. A source review found no AJP connector configuration anywhere in this repository.

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. Tomcat did not validate that the host name provided via the SNI extension was the same as the host name provided in the HTTP host header field. If Tomcat was configured with more than one virtual host and the TLS configuration for one of those hosts did not require client certificate authentication but another one did, it was possible for a client to bypass the client certificate authentication by sending different host names in the SNI extension and the HTTP host header field. The vulnerability only applies if client certificate authentication is only enforced at the Connector. This issue affects Apache Tomcat from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.14, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.49, from 9.0.0-M1 through 9.0.112, and 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.15 or later, 10.1.50 or later or 9.0.113 or later, which fix the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component configures TLS virtual hosts with connector-level client certificate authentication.

ratings.justification: The bypass needs multiple TLS virtual hosts with connector-level client certificate authentication; the only bundled Tomcat serves a single host over plain HTTP, and the Liquibase CLI never starts Tomcat.

analysis.detail: Client certificate authentication bypass through mismatched SNI and Host header names, fixed in Tomcat 11.0.15, 10.1.50 and 9.0.113. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2 and 10.1.48 in 5.0.3, both in range; 5.1.0 and later carry 11.0.15 or newer, which include the fix. The bypass needs a TLS connector serving more than one virtual host, with client certificate authentication required on the connector for one host but not another. The application sets no server properties, so its embedded Tomcat runs one default host over plain HTTP with no TLS connector and no client certificate authentication, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer.

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. Incorrect error handling for some invalid HTTP priority headers resulted in incomplete clean-up of the failed request which created a memory leak. A large number of such requests could trigger an OutOfMemoryException resulting in a denial of service. This issue affects Apache Tomcat from 9.0.76 through 9.0.102, from 10.1.10 through 10.1.39, from 11.0.0-M2 through 11.0.5, and 8.5.90 through 8.5.100. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.0.104, 10.1.40 or 11.0.6 which fix the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component enables HTTP/2 on Tomcat.

ratings.justification: The leak is in Tomcat's HTTP/2 priority handling; the only bundled Tomcat does not enable HTTP/2, and the Liquibase CLI never starts Tomcat.

analysis.detail: Memory leak on invalid HTTP priority headers, fixed in Tomcat 11.0.6, 10.1.40 and 9.0.104. The upstream fix changes only Tomcat's HTTP/2 implementation (org.apache.coyote.http2), so the leak is reachable only over HTTP/2. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. No other jar in the images contains Tomcat classes. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or newer, which include the fix. Spring Boot enables HTTP/2 only when server.http2.enabled is set; the application sets no server properties, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer, so its connector speaks HTTP/1.1 only.

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Neutralization of Escape, Meta, or Control Sequences vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. For a subset of unlikely rewrite rule configurations, it was possible for a specially crafted request to bypass some rewrite rules. If those rewrite rules effectively enforced security constraints, those constraints could be bypassed. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.5, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.39, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.102.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component configures a Tomcat RewriteValve.

ratings.justification: The bypass exists only in RewriteValve rule processing; no shipped component configures a RewriteValve, and the Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server.

analysis.detail: A crafted request can bypass some rewrite rules of Tomcat's RewriteValve; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.6, 10.1.40 and 9.0.104. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs a RewriteValve with rewrite rules. Spring Boot exposes no property that enables the RewriteValve; it must be added in code through a web server factory customizer together with a rewrite configuration. The application sets no server properties, packages no rewrite.config, and none of its classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer.

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's CGI servlet allows security constraint bypass of security constraints that apply to the pathInfo component of a URI mapped to the CGI servlet. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.6, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.40, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.104.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component enables the Tomcat CGI servlet.

ratings.justification: The bypass exists only for URIs mapped to the CGI servlet; no shipped component registers it, and the Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server.

analysis.detail: Case-sensitivity handling in Tomcat's CGI servlet allows a bypass of security constraints on the pathInfo of a URI mapped to that servlet; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.7, 10.1.41 and 9.0.105. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs the CGI servlet to be registered and mapped. Embedded Tomcat under Spring Boot does not load Tomcat's default web.xml and never registers the CGI servlet; the application registers only Spring's DispatcherServlet and none of its classes references CGIServlet or the Tomcat API.

vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted Search Path vulnerability in Apache Tomcat installer for Windows. During installation, the Tomcat installer for Windows used icacls.exe without specifying a full path. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.7, from 10.1.0 through 10.1.41, from 9.0.23 through 9.0.105.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not ship the Tomcat Windows installer.

ratings.justification: The flaw is in the Tomcat Windows installer, which no Liquibase Secure artifact contains; the embedded Tomcat library has no installer code.

analysis.detail: The Tomcat installer for Windows ran icacls.exe without a full path during installation; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.8, 10.1.42 and 9.0.106. The flaw is in the Windows installer executable distributed with the full Tomcat server download, not in the tomcat-embed-core library. No Liquibase Secure artifact ships or runs the Tomcat Windows installer. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the 5.x license-tracking application (10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer from 5.0.3), as a library inside that application's jar; it contains no installer code.

Information disclosure via padding oracle vulnerability in Tomcat EncryptInterceptor (clustering component). Requires Tomcat clustering with EncryptInterceptor enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; EncryptInterceptor is never instantiated.

vulnerabilities.description: Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. When using PreResources or PostResources mounted other than at the root of the web application, it was possible to access those resources via an unexpected path. That path was likely not to be protected by the same security constraints as the expected path, allowing those security constraints to be bypassed. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.7, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.41, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.105.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component mounts Tomcat PreResources or PostResources.

ratings.justification: The alternate path exists only for PreResources or PostResources mounted at a non-root path; no shipped component mounts any, and the Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server.

analysis.detail: Resources mounted as PreResources or PostResources other than at the web application root could be reached through an unexpected path that bypasses security constraints; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.8, 10.1.42 and 9.0.106. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs PreResources or PostResources mounted at a non-root path. Spring Boot exposes no property for this; it requires code that customizes the Tomcat context's WebResourceRoot. Spring Boot's own Tomcat setup adds only resource-jar sets mounted at the web application root, and only for jars that contain META-INF/resources, which none of the application's libraries do. None of the application's classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer, and the application bundles no Spring Security and defines no security constraints.

vulnerabilities.description: Session Fixation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat via rewrite valve. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.7, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.41, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.105.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. No shipped component configures a Tomcat RewriteValve.

ratings.justification: The session fixation exists only through the RewriteValve; no shipped component configures one, and the Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server.

analysis.detail: Session fixation through Tomcat's RewriteValve; fixed in Tomcat 11.0.8, 10.1.42 and 9.0.106. The Liquibase CLI never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core ships only as the embedded server of the license-tracking application, a separately started Spring Boot service shipped in 5.x and removed in 6.0.0. Docker images 5.0.0 through 5.2.2 carry it as an unextracted archive under /liquibase/dist (liquibase-license-tracking-1.0.0-beta.tar.gz). It runs only if a user extracts and starts it. The application carries tomcat-embed-core 10.1.34 in 5.0.0 to 5.0.2, which is in range; 5.0.3 and later carry 10.1.48 or 11.0.15 and newer, which include the fix. The flaw needs a RewriteValve. Spring Boot exposes no property that enables it; it must be added in code through a web server factory customizer. None of the application's classes references the Tomcat API or a web server factory customizer. The application is a stateless REST service and creates no HTTP sessions.

Information disclosure via improper encoding in Tomcat JsonAccessLogValve. Requires an active HTTP connector with JsonAccessLogValve configured and non-default relaxedPathChars/relaxedQueryChars values. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no access log valves are configured or initialized.

Information disclosure via sensitive data in Tomcat log files from the Kubernetes cloud membership provider (clustering). Requires Tomcat clustering with Kubernetes membership enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; Kubernetes cluster membership is never initialized.

Incomplete OCSP verification in Tomcat's FFM/OpenSSL TLS integration. Requires an active TLS listener with client certificate authentication and OCSP validation configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or binds any TLS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; the TLS and OCSP subsystems are never initialized.

vulnerabilities.description: Apache Tomcat RCE via Default Servlet partial PUT — file fragments uploaded to predictable temp paths trigger deserialization of assembled content. Also enables reading security-sensitive files.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: Server-side RCE requiring HTTP PUT to a running Tomcat servlet container. Liquibase never starts Tomcat or accepts HTTP requests.

analysis.detail: Remote code execution and information disclosure via Tomcat Default Servlet partial PUT support. Requires an HTTP PUT request to a running Tomcat servlet container with partial PUT enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts the Tomcat HTTP server, never deploys any servlet, and never opens any network port. The Default Servlet, partial PUT handling, and file session persistence code paths are never activated.

Denial of service via excessive memory consumption in Tomcat multipart upload processing. Requires sending a crafted multipart/form-data HTTP POST to a running Tomcat instance. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never accepts HTTP requests. The multipart parsing code path is completely inactive.

Denial of service via HTTP/2 stream reset memory leak in Tomcat. Requires an HTTP/2 connection to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and accepts no inbound network connections.
